issues.description: build_msd_circ usage: the problem statement and template expect the second-round distillation to be constructed by repeatedly using build_msd_circ on the next-available qubits (i.e., passing the next available qubit index). In the solution (solution_repository/msd.py) the second-round distilled_state is set to circ.num_qubits + 15 (line 271) instead of using the next available qubit index (circ.num_qubits). This produces a gap of 15 unused qubit indices between the existing circuit and the second-round distilled_state and leads to inconsistent circuit layout and measurement indexing. Concretely: the solution's first-round loop sets distilled_state = circ.num_qubits before each build_msd_circ call (solution_repository/msd.py line 258), but for the second round it chooses circ.num_qubits + 15 (solution_repository/msd.py line 271), which contradicts the pattern and the intended design described in the problem statement (problem_statement.md lines 167-176). This mismatch is likely to confuse students about how to pick the distilled_state index and can produce incorrect measurement indices in the assembled circuit.
issues.suggestedFix: When building the second round, pass the next available qubit index to build_msd_circ (use distilled_state = circ.num_qubits) or explicitly allocate the distilled_state qubit immediately before calling build_msd_circ so there is no unexplained gap. Ensure any subsequent indexing/measurement assumptions use the updated circ.num_qubits and adjust measurement-index bookkeeping accordingly so the tetrahedral ancilla block and the distilled data qubit are contiguous and consistent with the first-round pattern.
